standard_prerequisites.name: A finite type map from a Noetherian J-0 domain is smooth at the generic point when the fraction field extension is separable, and regularity ascends along smooth maps
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-smooth-at-generic-point} and Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-regular-goes-up}, cited at proof lines 11681-11683 and 11685-11686
standard_prerequisites.use: Give the smooothness at the generic point and regularity of the target.

core_obligations: Replace the source by a principal localisation so that it may be assumed regular (proof lines 11679-11680).
Use the generic smoothness statement to make the target smooth over the source after localising (proof lines 11681-11683).
Conclude regularity, hence the J-0 property, from ascent of regularity along smooth maps (proof lines 11684-11686).
proof_roadmap: Localise so the source is regular (proof lines 11679-11680).
Smoothness at the generic point (proof lines 11681-11683).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the J-0 property ascends: an injective finite type map from a Noetherian J-0 domain to a domain whose fraction field extension is separable has J-0 target. The proof replaces the source by a principal localisation, which is legitimate for verifying J-0, so that it may be assumed regular; then the map is smooth at the generic point, so after another principal localisation the target becomes smooth over the source, and smoothness makes the target regular, which is exactly the J-0 condition in the localised situation.
